n: Alma turns to his youngest son, Corianton, with more to say. He points to Shiblon’s steady, faithful example and asks whether it hasn’t set a good pattern for Corianton.
Corianton didn’t listen to his father as well as Shiblon did during the Zoramite mission. He started boasting in his own strength and wisdom.
Worse, Corianton abandoned his mission and went to Siron, near Lamanite lands, to pursue a prostitute named Isabel. This deeply grieved his father.
Isabel led many astray, but Alma tells Corianton that’s no excuse. He should have stayed focused on the work entrusted to him.
Alma teaches the seriousness of sexual sin: in God’s eyes it is more abominable than any sin except murder and denying the Holy Ghost. Sacred powers of creation are meant for marriage.

f.g: Something God regards as deeply offensive.

n: Denying the Holy Ghost after having received it and knowing what one is doing is unforgivable. Murder against the light of God is also very hard to be forgiven.
Alma wishes Corianton had never committed so serious a sin. He wouldn’t bring it up at all if it weren’t for Corianton’s good.

f.g: Stir up deep distress, as a harrow tears up soil.

n: Sins can’t be hidden from God. Unless they are repented of, they will testify against a person at the final judgment.

f.w: ye cannot hide your crimes from God

n: Alma pleads with Corianton to repent, forsake his sins, stop following the “lusts of his eyes,” and “cross himself”—deny himself these desires. Without this he cannot inherit God’s kingdom.

f.g: Deny yourself; resist your own desires.

n: Corianton is to counsel with his older brothers, Helaman and Shiblon. Being young, he needs their support and should heed their advice.
Don’t let vain or foolish things lead you away again. Corianton’s behavior had a painful consequence: the Zoramites saw it and refused to believe Alma’s message.

f.w: when they saw your conduct they would not believe

n: The Spirit tells Alma to command his children to do good so they don’t lead others to destruction. So he solemnly commands Corianton to stop his sins.
Turn to the Lord with all your mind, might, and strength. Lead no one else into sin; go back to the people, admit your faults, and try to make it right.

f.w: with all your mind, might, and strength

n: Don’t chase wealth or worldly things—you can’t take them with you.

f.w: you cannot carry them with you

n: Alma moves from rebuke to hope. Christ will surely come to take away the sins of the world—including Corianton’s—and bring glad tidings of salvation.

f.w: take away the sins of the world

n: That message was exactly what Corianton had been called to preach: preparing the people—and their children—for Christ’s coming.
Corianton apparently wondered why Christ’s coming should be announced so far in advance. Alma answers: isn’t a soul today just as precious to God as one living when Christ comes?

f.w: a soul at this time as precious

n: Doesn’t this generation need to know the plan of redemption as much as their children will?
And isn’t it just as easy for God to send angels with this good news now as later? God loves every generation equally.

f.w: send his angel to declare these glad tidings
